--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Add multiple nodes to the graph in a single call. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Add multiple nodes to the graph in a single call. title: >- [Graph.add_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Add multiple nodes to the graph in a single call. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add multiple nodes to the graph in a single call. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1552-L1745){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_nodes( nodes, type=None, **shared_attrs, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Add several nodes](../assets/graphs/add-nodes.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: a four-node cycle A, B, D, C. After: two new nodes, E and F, appear in the accent color beside it in one call, with no edges; nothing else changes." width="100%"} A bulk version of `add_node()` that accepts a list of node labels and applies shared attributes to all of them. Individual nodes can override shared attributes by passing a tuple of `(label, dict)` instead of a bare label, or the whole argument can be a dict mapping each label to its attributes. Nodes are added in the order given, each receiving the next auto-assigned ID, and every label is converted to a string (so `range(1, 4)` produces the labels `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`). The nodes are created without edges; follow up with `add_edges()` to connect them. The whole call is recorded as a single step in the step log (see `steps`), which keeps `play()` replays compact. This is the natural way to: - declare the vertex set of a graph up front, before adding edges - tag a batch of nodes with a common `type=` or shared attributes - create numbered nodes quickly from a `range` Labels are unique: if any label is already in the graph, or appears twice in `nodes=`, a `ValueError` is raised before any node is added. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[list, range]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node labels to add, as a list (or any iterable such as a `range` or a generator). Each element can be: - A string or int label (e.g., `'Alice'`, `42`), converted to a string label. - A tuple of `(label, attrs_dict)` to override shared attributes for that node. The dict is merged on top of `**shared_attrs=`, and may contain a `"type"` key to override `type=` for that node. Alternatively, pass a dict mapping each label to its attribute dict (or `None` for none), e.g. `{'Alice': {'team': 'red'}, 'Bob': None}`. A tuple that isn't `(label, dict)`, or a non-dict attribute value, raises a `TypeError`; the input is checked before any node is added. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional type applied to every node (unless overridden per-node with a `"type"` key in the attributes dict). Stored in the first-class `type` column of the node DataFrame. Default is `None`, which leaves the type unset. [**shared_attrs]{.doc-parameter-name} : Attributes applied to every node (unless overridden per-node), e.g., `team="red"`. Each key becomes a column in the node DataFrame. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns self to enable method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a label already exists in the graph or repeats within `nodes=`. [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an element is a tuple other than `(label, attrs_dict)`, is itself a dict, or (with the dict form) a node's attributes aren't a dict or `None`. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~add_node`) : Add one node. [](`~add_edges`) : Add many edges at once. [](`~from_edges`) : Build a graph straight from an edge list. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Add several nodes at once with a shared type. Every node gets `type="person"` and sequential IDs: ::: {#91973aaa .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["Alice", "Bob", "Carol"], type="person") graph.get_node_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 4)
idlabeltypedegree
i64strstri64
1"Alice""person"0
2"Bob""person"0
3"Carol""person"0
``` ::: ::: Shared keyword attributes apply to all nodes, while a `(label, dict)` tuple overrides them for a single node. Here Bob becomes an admin on a different team, and Carol a bot: ::: {#d943a239 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes( [ "Alice", ("Bob", {"role": "admin", "team": "blue"}), ("Carol", {"type": "bot"}), ], type="person", team="red", ) graph.get_node_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 6)
idlabeltyperoleteamdegree
i64strstrstrstri64
1"Alice""person"null"red"0
2"Bob""person""admin""blue"0
3"Carol""bot"null"red"0
``` ::: ::: A dict maps each label to its own attributes, which reads naturally when every node has different values: ::: {#01dad75d .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes( {"Alice": {"age": 34}, "Bob": {"age": 27}, "Carol": None}, type="person", ) graph.get_node_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 5)
idlabeltypeagedegree
i64strstri64i64
1"Alice""person"340
2"Bob""person"270
3"Carol""person"null0
``` ::: ::: Use a range for numeric node labels. Note that the labels are stored as strings: ::: {#fd3d11d7 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(range(1, 6)) graph.get_node_df()["label"].to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['1', '2', '3', '4', '5'] ``` ::: ::: ### Accounts before payments A bank's accounts come from one table and its payments from another. Adding the accounts first, as `(label, attrs)` tuples made from the table's rows, keeps an account that has made no payments yet: ::: {#99906f46 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl accounts = pl.DataFrame( { "name": [ "Acme", "Dee", "Eve", "Ana", "Grocer", "Cafe", "Landlord" ], "kind": ["business"] + ["person"] * 3 + ["business"] * 3, } ) nodes = [(name, {"kind": kind}) for name, kind in accounts.iter_rows()] bank = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(nodes) .add_edges( [ ("Acme", "Dee"), ("Acme", "Eve"), ("Dee", "Eve"), ("Ana", "Dee"), ("Dee", "Grocer"), ("Eve", "Grocer"), ("Ana", "Grocer"), ("Eve", "Cafe"), ] ) ) bank.plot(color_by="kind", label_by="label", seed=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The Landlord has no payments this month, so it stands apart. Built from the payments alone, the graph wouldn't have it at all.
